## Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted}

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{marginfigure}
\resizebox{0.92\linewidth}{!}{\mlphysicalstackfull{20}{20}{20}{20}{20}}
\end{marginfigure}
:::

_Why can a machine pass its normal operating tests and still fail when its protective response is needed?_

The claims that matter most in a physical machine describe what it does after something has already gone wrong, when the learned proposer stalls, an observation arrives old, a message is lost, or the supply sags while a loaded body moves toward a person. Normal operation almost never exercises those responses, so thousands of clean runs can coexist with a stopping mechanism that has never once been made to stop the machine. Without deliberate testing, the first real trial of that mechanism happens in service, where a late response delivers energy that no software correction can recall. Establishing such a claim requires creating the fault on purpose, measuring the physical response with instruments the fault cannot reach, and scoring it against acceptance conditions fixed before the test, and every condition left untested still limits what the result can support. Verification makes those limits explicit before release grants any action authority to cross the causal boundary.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {.callout-learning-objectives}

- Derive test conditions and stopping oracles from the machine's operating envelope
- Derive faults from design assumptions, physical hazards, and authority-transfer failures
- Select qualification environments that exercise the causal mechanism behind each claim
- Design hardware injections with independent witnesses and precommitted acceptance conditions
- Interpret temporal safety margins and search for disturbances that violate them
- Evaluate the assumptions limiting simulation transfer, rare-event estimates, and formal proofs
- Assemble fault records that preserve failed, invalid, unobservable, and untested cases

:::
## The Claim a Fault Trial Must Test {#sec-verification-fault-injection}

Every earlier chapter of this book ends in claims about the running machine, such as a lease that expires within its bound, a permission path that stops the base inside its clearance, or a safety microcontroller that outlives a brownout of the shared supply. Verification is the discipline that turns such claims into evidence. In a physical AI system its difficulty is specific. The claims that matter most describe the machine's protective response, and that response runs only after something has already failed. Normal operation rarely exercises it, and a failure first discovered in service has already delivered energy across the causal boundary that no correction can recall. The protective response must therefore be exercised deliberately, before release, under the conditions that make it necessary.

::: {.column-margin}
![](images/svg/spa_locator_as.svg){width="100%" fig-alt="S·P·A locator triad highlighting the Act-to-Sense feedback edge."}

*A trial passes only when an independent sensor witnesses the act.*
:::

Policy evaluation in @sec-evaluation asks how well a learned candidate performs under declared tasks and conditions. Here the object under test is the assembled machine: proposer, permission path, communication, power, and body. A strong evaluation result does not establish that an independent stop still works when the proposer stalls. Conversely, a successful protective stop does not show that the policy completes its task well. Release needs both kinds of evidence for the same configuration. The same distinction separates proposer autonomy from whole-machine task success, because a permitted least-change correction can preserve successful service while exposing a limitation of the raw proposal.

The **digital twin delusion**\index{Digital twin delusion!simulation limits}[^fn-digital-twin-origin] treats passing simulated assertions as sufficient evidence for physical safety. A simulator can represent timing, electrical, and contact effects only to the extent that its models include and validate them. An omitted power fault cannot fail a simulated controller. Operational logs invite the corresponding mistake. Incident-free exposure, however long, leaves unencountered faults untested.

[^fn-digital-twin-origin]: **Digital Twin**\index{Digital twin!origin}: @grieves2017digital trace the concept to a 2002 presentation on product lifecycle management, and @glaessgen2012digital gave it the sense aerospace adopted, a simulation of one as-built vehicle, updated continually from that vehicle's own sensors and history so that it mirrors the life of its flying twin. The original meaning therefore depended on continual calibration against one particular physical article. A simulator that has never been compared with a measured stop of this machine is a model, not a twin, and treating it as a twin is the delusion this chapter names.

**Adversarial fault injection** turns a claim into a deliberate disturbance under independent physical containment. The central question is what such a trial must contain for its result to count as evidence, and how far a finite set of trials can reach. We answer it in the order an engineer builds a campaign: the operating envelope in which the claim should hold; one fully specified trial, with the precommitted oracle that scores it and the fault record that preserves it; the extension of that trial across the envelope's coupled conditions; the faults derived from the design's premises and from the physical machine; the test environment that contains each fault's mechanism; the hardware on which injection becomes real; the searches and statistics that extend a handful of trials; and the records that carry both the evidence and its limits to release.

```{python}
#| label: calc-verify-rack-end-oracle
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ RACK-END FAULT-INJECTION ORACLE FOR THE RUNNING MACHINE (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: fault-injection scene, operating envelope, fault list, oracles,
# │          hardware injection, fault manifest, fallacies, and summary.
# │ Goal: Derive the two oracle bounds (powered deceleration onset after the last valid renewal,
# │       stopping distance at the aisle speed) and the envelope points that
# │       F1-F4 and A1-A4 are injected at, all from the machine's registry entry.
# │ Show: 82 ms onset bound; 969.0 mm budget and 131.0 mm spare at 1.3 m/s;
# │       100.8 ms of travel in that spare, 751.6 ms at the 0.75 m/s takeover
# │       speed; the 1.44 m/s dry and 1.23 m/s inspected-floor ceilings; the
# │       37.8 V sustained drive-bus sag, 4.8 V above the 33 V converter
# │       lockout (150 A to cross it); the permission rail's 2.0 s hold-up against
# │       1313.43 ms from flag to brakes set (F4b); F1's stop oracle from the
# │       last valid renewal (751.9 mm at 1.3 m/s); the F1 record's oracle at
# │       the restricted 1.0 m/s point (629.6 mm from the last valid renewal);
# │       the Class 3 tank contrast (volume, not distance); F2's refusal
# │       threshold, the 51.6 ms budgeted dispatch age plus the 0.2 ms clock-conversion
# │       bound (51.8 ms upper age); the unbudgeted queue length that exhausts
# │       the spare (100.8 ms, about three-quarters of the pre-brake subtotal);
# │       a late-onset F1 trace's signed and normalized margins; the SoC's share
# │       of the bus transient (1.6 A of 70 A); the discrepancy a spare-sized
# │       simulated margin tolerates (0.131 in a 1 m position norm); the visible
# │       arithmetic of the reference-event notebook (217.1 mm between the capture-
# │       referenced subtotal and the F1 oracle) and the supply-headroom notebook
# │       (headroom vanishes near 129 mOhm); checkpoint givens (a 90 ms onset).
# │ How: the jerk-limited S-curve stop (calc_scurve_stop_distance / _time,
# │      calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity) with the jerk bound taken as the
# │      reference C2 polynomial's peak jerk at the drive limit, as in
# │      @sec-planning-c2-stopping-suffix, and the three fixed overheads;
# │      calc_voltage_droop for the 48 V drive bus (M6); tank arithmetic by
# │      conservation of volume.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import ureg, kilogram, microsecond, millisecond, second, meter, millimeter
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import (
    calc_c2_stop_suffix,
    calc_scurve_stop_distance,
    calc_scurve_stop_time,
    calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity,
)
from mlsysim.physics import calc_voltage_droop
from mlsysim.fmt import (
    fmt,
    fmt_latency,
    fmt_time,
    fmt_length,
    fmt_velocity,
    fmt_acceleration,
    fmt_voltage,
    fmt_current,
    fmt_temperature,
    fmt_mass,
    fmt_percent,
    fmt_power,
    fmt_int,
    fmt_resistance,
    fmt_display_math,
    check,
)

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

def _num(q, unit, p):
    # Plain magnitude for the notebooks' visible arithmetic (no thousands separator inside math);
    # integer-like values print without a decimal, others at precision p
    x = q.to(unit).magnitude
    if abs(x - round(x)) < 1e-9:
        return fmt_int(round(x), commas=False)
    return fmt(x, precision=p, commas=False)

class RackEndVerification:
    """Oracle bounds and envelope points for fault injection at the rack end."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    v_aisle = AISLE.v_aisle  # category: chosen
    v_drive = RM.base.max_velocity  # category: illustrative
    a_brake = AISLE.a_brake  # category: illustrative
    tau_delay = AISLE.tau_delay  # category: derived
    t_age = AISLE.perception_age  # category: derived
    eps_sync = 0.2 * millisecond  # category: illustrative (clock-conversion bound, @sec-perception-observation-contract)
    t_lease = AISLE.t_lease  # category: chosen
    t_tick = AISLE.t_tick  # category: chosen
    t_bus = AISLE.t_bus  # category: illustrative
    t_act = AISLE.t_brake_onset  # category: illustrative
    heartbeat_timeout = AISLE.heartbeat_timeout  # category: chosen
    enforcer_deadline = AISLE.enforcer_deadline  # category: chosen
    chunk_rate = RM.chunk_rate  # category: chosen
    t_takeover = AISLE.t_takeover_in_loop  # category: derived (sourced reaction, video, and handshake terms; M4)
    v_takeover = AISLE.v_takeover_in_loop  # category: derived (Delta_da-charged in-loop ceiling, rounded down; Ch14)
    d_clear = AISLE.d_clear  # category: illustrative
    delta_loc = AISLE.delta_loc  # category: illustrative
    delta_margin = AISLE.delta_margin  # category: chosen
    eps_track = AISLE.eps_track  # category: illustrative
    side_clearance = AISLE.side_clearance  # category: illustrative
    mu_dry = AISLE.mu_dry  # category: illustrative
    mu_insp = AISLE.mu_inspected_floor  # category: illustrative
    payload = RM.onboard_payload_capacity  # category: chosen
    bus_nominal = RM.drive_bus_nominal  # category: datasheet (48 V-class pack, nominal)
    bus_low = RM.drive_bus_battery_low  # category: datasheet (pack minimum)
    bus_r = RM.drive_bus_resistance  # category: illustrative (source path; needs a measured value)
    bus_uvlo = RM.drive_bus_uvlo  # category: datasheet (converter input lockout)
    i_rail = AISLE.i_rail_transient  # category: illustrative
    rail_holdup = RM.permission_rail_holdup  # category: chosen
    brake_engage_max = RM.spring_brake_engage_max  # category: illustrative
    g = (1 * ureg.standard_gravity).to(meter / second**2)  # physical constant (defined); category: derived
    # Scenario assumptions local to this chapter
    ambient_lo = ureg.Quantity(5.0, ureg.degC)  # scenario assumption; category: chosen
    ambient_hi = ureg.Quantity(35.0, ureg.degC)  # scenario assumption; category: chosen
    lease_probe = 5 * millisecond  # proposal injected after expiry; scenario assumption; category: chosen
    v_restricted = (
        1.0 * meter / second
    )  # restricted-mode aisle speed on inspected floors, below the inspected-floor ceiling; scenario assumption; category: chosen
    late_onset = 30 * millisecond  # example late powered deceleration onset (STL margin); scenario assumption; category: illustrative
    chk_onset = 90 * millisecond  # checkpoint given: a measured onset after the last valid renewal; scenario assumption; category: illustrative
    soc_power = RM.brain_soc.tdp_max  # category: datasheet (application SoC maximum module power)
    converter_eff = RM.drive_bus_converter_efficiency  # category: datasheet (typical converter efficiency)
    drive_current_limit = RM.drive_current_limit  # category: chosen (per-motor datasheet peak)
    drive_wheels = RM.drive_wheel_count  # category: chosen

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    overhead = (delta_loc + delta_margin + eps_track).to(millimeter)
    # Jerk bound: the reference C2 polynomial's peak jerk at the drive limit (@sec-planning-c2-stopping-suffix)
    j_brake = calc_c2_stop_suffix(v_drive, a_brake)["peak_jerk"].to(meter / second**3)
    onset_bound = (t_lease + t_tick + t_bus + t_act).to(millisecond)
    upper_age = (t_age + eps_sync).to(millisecond)  # F2: dispatch-only upper-age threshold; admission/execution age continues
    lease_probe_at = (t_lease + lease_probe).to(millisecond)
    chunk_period = (1 / chunk_rate).to(millisecond)
    c2_distance = calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_aisle, a_brake, j_brake).to(millimeter)
    budget = (v_aisle * tau_delay + c2_distance + overhead).to(millimeter)
    spare = (d_clear - budget).to(millimeter)
    t_spare = (spare / v_aisle).to(millisecond)
    per_ms = (v_aisle * (1 * millisecond)).to(millimeter)
    budget_takeover = (v_takeover * tau_delay + calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_takeover, a_brake, j_brake) + overhead).to(millimeter)
    spare_takeover = (d_clear - budget_takeover).to(millimeter)
    t_spare_takeover = (spare_takeover / v_takeover).to(millisecond)
    ceiling_dry = calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
        d_clear, tau_delay, a_brake, j_brake, loc_margin=delta_loc, physical_margin=delta_margin + eps_track
    ).to(meter / second)
    mu_min = float((a_brake / g).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    # The floor caps the deceleration; the jerk bound belongs to the load and is unchanged.
    a_insp = min(a_brake, (mu_insp * g).to(meter / second**2))
    budget_insp = (v_aisle * tau_delay + calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_aisle, a_insp, j_brake) + overhead).to(millimeter)
    ceiling_insp = calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
        d_clear, tau_delay, a_insp, j_brake, loc_margin=delta_loc, physical_margin=delta_margin + eps_track
    ).to(meter / second)
    bus_sag = calc_voltage_droop(i_rail, bus_r).to(ureg.volt)
    bus_min = (bus_low - bus_sag).to(ureg.volt)  # sustained screen from the depleted pack
    bus_margin = (bus_min - bus_uvlo).to(ureg.volt)
    i_cross = ((bus_low - bus_uvlo) / bus_r).to(ureg.ampere)  # step that would reach the lockout
    # F4: from the undervoltage or feed-loss flag, stop onset, the longest resident
    # stop inside the envelope (inspected floor at its ceiling), and brakes set
    flag_onset = (t_tick + t_bus + t_act).to(millisecond)
    stop_insp_ceiling = calc_scurve_stop_time(ceiling_insp, a_insp, j_brake).to(millisecond)
    flag_to_set = (flag_onset + stop_insp_ceiling + brake_engage_max).to(millisecond)
    holdup_margin = (rail_holdup - flag_to_set).to(millisecond)
    # F1 record at the restricted point, scored from the last valid renewal
    f1_preonset = (v_restricted * onset_bound).to(millimeter)
    f1_c2 = calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_restricted, a_insp, j_brake).to(millimeter)
    f1_stop_bound = (f1_preonset + f1_c2 + eps_track).to(millimeter)
    # F1 at the aisle speed, scored from the same event (last valid renewal)
    f1_aisle_stop_bound = (v_aisle * onset_bound + c2_distance + eps_track).to(millimeter)
    budget_restricted = (v_restricted * tau_delay + f1_c2 + overhead).to(millimeter)
    late_extra = (v_aisle * late_onset).to(millimeter)
    # Signed margins of one late-onset F1 trace against the renewal-referenced oracle
    onset_late = (onset_bound + late_onset).to(millisecond)
    travel_late = (f1_aisle_stop_bound + late_extra).to(millimeter)
    rho_onset = (onset_bound - onset_late).to(millisecond)
    rho_dist = (f1_aisle_stop_bound - travel_late).to(millimeter)
    # Normalized by chosen scales equal to the bounds themselves
    rho_onset_n = float((rho_onset / onset_bound).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    rho_dist_n = float((rho_dist / f1_aisle_stop_bound).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    # Notebook nbk-verification-reference-event-gap: both sums term by term
    f1_preonset_aisle = (v_aisle * onset_bound).to(millimeter)
    capture_preonset = (v_aisle * tau_delay).to(millimeter)
    age_travel = (v_aisle * t_age).to(millimeter)
    ref_gap = (budget - f1_aisle_stop_bound).to(millimeter)
    late_equiv = (ref_gap / v_aisle).to(millisecond)  # onset slip the distance predicate alone would absorb
    sfx_v2 = (v_aisle**2 / (2 * a_brake)).to(meter)  # d_suffix, braking term (@eq-plan-c2-stopping-suffix)
    sfx_jerk = (v_aisle * a_brake / (2 * j_brake)).to(meter)  # d_suffix, jerk-ramp term
    sfx_v2_r = (v_restricted**2 / (2 * a_insp)).to(meter)
    sfx_jerk_r = (v_restricted * a_insp / (2 * j_brake)).to(meter)
    speed_cut = 1.0 - float((v_restricted / v_aisle).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    oracle_cut = 1.0 - float((f1_stop_bound / f1_aisle_stop_bound).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    # Notebook nbk-verification-supply-headroom: stop time T = v/a + a/j from the inspected-floor ceiling
    tstop_va = (ceiling_insp / a_insp).to(millisecond)
    tstop_aj = (a_insp / j_brake).to(millisecond)
    r_cross = ((bus_low - bus_uvlo) / i_rail).to(ureg.milliohm)  # source resistance at which the transient alone reaches lockout
    step_ratio = float((i_cross / i_rail).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    # Checkpoint given: onset and pre-braking travel of a late F1 onset
    chk_rho = (onset_bound - chk_onset).to(millisecond)
    chk_extra = (v_aisle * (chk_onset - onset_bound)).to(millimeter)
    # Shared-bus sag attribution: the application SoC's maximum draw from the depleted bus
    soc_current = (soc_power / (bus_low * converter_eff)).to(ureg.ampere)
    drive_peak = (drive_current_limit * drive_wheels).to(ureg.ampere)
    soc_share = float((soc_current / i_rail).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    # Sim-to-real instance: position error in meters (L_phi = 1 m per unit of the norm);
    # a simulated margin equal to the spare tolerates at most this discrepancy
    eps_gap_max = float((spare / (1 * meter)).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    # Fallacy: an unbudgeted queue spends the spare at v per unit time, so the
    # queue length that exhausts it is the spare's travel time t_spare.
    queue_exhaust_ratio = (t_spare / tau_delay).to("dimensionless").magnitude

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Assertions) ────────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(onset_bound.magnitude - 82.0) < 1e-9, "Canon: powered deceleration onset 82 ms after the last valid renewal.")
    check(abs(tau_delay.to(millisecond).magnitude - 133.6) < 5e-3, "Canon: tau_delay 133.6 ms.")
    check(abs(t_age.to(millisecond).magnitude - 51.6) < 5e-3, "Canon: t_age 51.6 ms.")
    check(abs(eps_sync.to(millisecond).magnitude - 0.2) < 1e-9, "Clock-conversion bound must match the perception contract's 0.2 ms.")
    check(abs(upper_age.magnitude - 51.8) < 5e-3, "Canon (D22): F2 dispatch-age check refuses above a 51.8 ms upper age.")
    check(abs(j_brake.magnitude - 64.0 / 9.0) < 1e-9, "Canon: the jerk bound is the reference polynomial's 7.11 m/s^3 peak.")
    check(abs(budget.magnitude - 968.9925) < 5e-3, "Canon: budget at 1.3 m/s is 968.99 mm.")
    check(abs(spare.magnitude - 131.0075) < 5e-3, "Canon: spare at 1.3 m/s is 131.01 mm.")
    check(abs(c2_distance.magnitude - 605.3125) < 5e-3, "Canon: S-curve stop at 1.3 m/s is 605.31 mm.")
    check(abs(t_spare.magnitude - 100.775) < 5e-3, "Canon: T_latest 100.8 ms.")
    check(abs(ceiling_dry.magnitude - 1.4367) < 5e-5, "Canon: dry-floor ceiling 1.4367 m/s.")
    check(abs(ceiling_insp.magnitude - 1.2309) < 5e-5, "Canon: inspected-floor ceiling 1.2309 m/s.")
    check(abs(mu_min - 0.204) < 5e-4, "Canon: friction needed for a_brake is 0.204.")
    check(abs(bus_min.magnitude - 37.8) < 5e-3, "Canon: the depleted drive bus sags to 37.8 V.")
    check(abs(bus_margin.magnitude - 4.8) < 5e-3, "The sustained screen leaves 4.8 V above the converter lockout.")
    check(abs(i_cross.magnitude - 150.0) < 1e-6, "Reaching the lockout takes a 150 A step.")
    check(bus_min > bus_uvlo, "The load alone cannot cross the lockout, so F4a must inject a supply dip.")
    check(v_aisle < ceiling_dry and ceiling_insp < v_aisle, "Aisle speed sits between the two ceilings.")
    check(budget_insp > d_clear, "At the aisle speed the inspected-floor budget must exceed the clear distance.")
    check(mu_insp < mu_min < mu_dry, "Dry floor supports a_brake; the inspected floor does not.")
    check(t_spare < tau_delay, "A queue shorter than the budgeted pre-brake subtotal exhausts the spare.")
    check(abs(queue_exhaust_ratio - 0.754) < 5e-4, "The exhausting queue is about three-quarters of the pre-brake subtotal.")
    check(abs(overhead.magnitude - 190.0) < 1e-6, "Canon: fixed overhead 190 mm.")
    check(rho_onset.magnitude < 0 and rho_dist.magnitude < 0, "A late onset must drive both F1 margins negative.")
    check(abs(rho_onset_n + 30.0 / 82.0) < 1e-9, "Normalized onset margin is -30/82.")
    check(rho_onset_n < rho_dist_n < 0, "The onset margin dominates the normalized minimum.")
    check(soc_current < 0.05 * i_rail, "The SoC draws a few percent of the rail transient; drive current dominates.")
    check(drive_peak <= i_rail, "Two drive motors at their peak supply most of the transient.")
    check(abs(eps_gap_max - spare.to(meter).magnitude) < 1e-12, "Tolerable discrepancy equals the spare in meters.")
    check(abs(v_takeover.to(meter / second).magnitude - 0.75) < 1e-9, "Canon: in-loop takeover speed 0.75 m/s (derived, Ch14).")
    check(
        t_spare_takeover >= t_takeover + AISLE.t_dispatch_to_admission, "At the slowed speed the spare must cover the in-loop takeover and Delta_da."
    )
    check(t_spare < t_takeover, "At the aisle speed the spare cannot cover the in-loop takeover.")
    check(abs(spare_takeover.magnitude - 563.71) < 5e-2, "Canon: spare at the 0.75 m/s takeover speed is 563.7 mm.")
    check(abs(t_spare_takeover.magnitude - 751.6) < 5e-2, "Canon: T_latest 751.6 ms at 0.75 m/s.")
    check(abs(flag_onset.magnitude - 22.0) < 1e-9, "Canon: stop onset within 22 ms of the flag.")
    check(abs(rail_holdup.to(second).magnitude - 2.0) < 1e-9, "Canon: permission-rail hold-up 2.0 s.")
    check(abs(flag_to_set.magnitude - 1313.43) < 5e-3, "Canon: flag to brakes set 1313.43 ms.")
    check(abs(holdup_margin.magnitude - 686.57) < 5e-3, "Canon: hold-up margin 686.57 ms.")
    check(v_restricted < ceiling_insp, "The restricted point must sit below the inspected-floor ceiling.")
    check(abs(f1_preonset.magnitude - 82.0) < 1e-6, "Canon: 82 mm of pre-onset travel at 1.0 m/s.")
    check(abs(f1_c2.magnitude - 507.6) < 5e-2, "Canon: S-curve stop at 1.0 m/s on the inspected floor is 507.6 mm.")
    check(abs(f1_stop_bound.magnitude - 629.6) < 5e-2, "Canon: F1 stop oracle 629.6 mm from the last valid renewal.")
    check(
        abs(f1_aisle_stop_bound.magnitude - 751.9125) < 5e-3 and f1_aisle_stop_bound < budget,
        "F1 stop oracle at 1.3 m/s is 751.91 mm from the last valid renewal.",
    )
    check(
        abs(budget_restricted.magnitude - 831.2) < 5e-2 and budget_restricted < d_clear,
        "Canon: budget at 1.0 m/s on the inspected floor is 831.2 mm.",
    )
    # margin_renewal_onset_deadline_bar.svg fig-alt hand-types 60, 1, 1, and 20 ms (82 ms guarded above)
    check(
        abs(t_lease.to(millisecond).magnitude - 60.0) < 1e-9
        and abs(t_tick.to(millisecond).magnitude - 1.0) < 1e-9
        and abs(t_bus.to(millisecond).magnitude - 1.0) < 1e-9
        and abs(t_act.to(millisecond).magnitude - 20.0) < 1e-9,
        "Onset-bar fig-alt: lease 60 ms, tick 1 ms, bus 1 ms, onset 20 ms.",
    )
    # margin_floor_friction_ceiling_knee.svg fig-alt hand-types mu 0.12 and 1.3 m/s (0.204, 1.44, 1.23 guarded above)
    check(abs(mu_insp - 0.12) < 1e-9 and abs(v_aisle.to(meter / second).magnitude - 1.3) < 1e-9, "Knee fig-alt: mu 0.12, aisle 1.3 m/s.")
    # Reference-event notebook: the closed-form stop matches the MLSysIM S-curve, and the
    # capture-referenced subtotal exceeds the F1 oracle by exactly age travel plus the two margins
    check(abs((sfx_v2 + sfx_jerk).to(millimeter).magnitude - c2_distance.magnitude) < 1e-6, "d_suffix = v^2/2a + v a/2j at 1.3 m/s.")
    check(abs((sfx_v2_r + sfx_jerk_r).to(millimeter).magnitude - f1_c2.magnitude) < 1e-6, "d_suffix = v^2/2a + v a/2j at 1.0 m/s.")
    check(v_restricted > a_insp**2 / j_brake and v_aisle > a_brake**2 / j_brake, "Both stops reach the deceleration plateau.")
    check(
        abs(ref_gap.magnitude - (age_travel + delta_loc + delta_margin).to(millimeter).magnitude) < 1e-6,
        "Gap = age travel + delta_loc + delta_margin.",
    )
    check(
        abs(ref_gap.magnitude - 217.08) < 5e-3 and 2 * onset_bound < late_equiv < 2.1 * onset_bound,
        "The 217.1 mm gap hides about twice the onset bound.",
    )
    check(abs(speed_cut - 0.231) < 5e-4 and abs(oracle_cut - 0.163) < 5e-4, "A 23 percent slower point shortens the oracle 16 percent.")
    check(abs((tstop_va + tstop_aj - stop_insp_ceiling).magnitude) < 1e-6, "Stop time T = v/a + a/j at the inspected ceiling.")
    check(
        abs(r_cross.magnitude - 128.571) < 5e-3 and 2.0 < step_ratio < 2.2,
        "Headroom vanishes near 129 mOhm; the crossing step is about twice the transient.",
    )
    check(
        float((rho_dist / eps_track).to("dimensionless").magnitude) < rho_onset_n,
        "Checkpoint: with the 40 mm inset as distance scale, distance sets the combined score.",
    )
    check(abs(chk_rho.magnitude + 8.0) < 1e-9 and abs(chk_extra.magnitude - 10.4) < 1e-6, "Checkpoint: 90 ms onset misses by 8 ms and adds 10.4 mm.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Format & Export) ────────────────────────────────────────
    v_aisle_str = fmt_velocity(v_aisle, precision=1)

    onset_math = fmt_display_math(

        rf" = {_num(age_travel, _mm, 1)} + {_num(delta_loc + delta_margin, _mm, 0)} = {_num(ref_gap, _mm, 1)}\ \text{{mm}}"

    restricted_math = fmt_display_math(

        rf" = {_num(flag_onset, _ms, 0)} + \left(\frac{{{_num(ceiling_insp, _mps, 3)}}}{{{_num(a_insp, _mps2, 3)}}} + \frac{{{_num(a_insp, _mps2, 3)}}}{{{j_brake_str}}}\right)\text{{s}} + {_num(brake_engage_max, _ms, 0)}"
        rf" = {_num(flag_onset, _ms, 0)} + {_num(tstop_va, _ms, 1)} + {_num(tstop_aj, _ms, 1)} + {_num(brake_engage_max, _ms, 0)} = {_num(flag_to_set, _ms, 1)}\ \text{{ms}}"
```
