: **Fault-record set for release**: The schema of the signed set in which the fault record reaches release, defining the multi-dimensional empirical evidence required to support operational release. {#tbl-15-verification-matrix-contract tbl-colwidths="[20,18,34,28]"}
## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-verification-fallacies-pitfalls}

A machine can pass every isolated fault test and still fail when a shared rail, bus, or clock couples the faults or disables their detectors. These failures stem from **unintended causal, electrical, and temporal coupling** across architectural boundaries. Compound tests catch such failures only when enough galvanically or logically independent instrumentation survives the fault to establish the sequence of events.\index{Fault coupling!shared resources}

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Independent local watchdog timers guarantee end-to-end physical deadline compliance.*

A sensor, proposer, and permission path can each meet its local execution deadline while an unmonitored queue holds the observation between them. The watchdogs measure time spent inside their own tasks; the stopping claim depends on elapsed time across the complete path.

For an illustrative violation, add an unbudgeted queue to the running machine's `{python} RackEndVerification.tau_delay_str` pre-deceleration budget. At `{python} RackEndVerification.v_aisle_str`, every millisecond of queueing adds `{python} RackEndVerification.per_ms_str` of travel, so a queue of `{python} RackEndVerification.t_spare_str` spends the whole `{python} RackEndVerification.spare_str` reserve, and any longer queue breaches the clear-distance budget. That queue is only `{python} RackEndVerification.queue_exhaust_pct_str` of the budgeted pre-deceleration interval, and every local watchdog still passes while it grows. The reserve has not yet paid for dispatch-to-admission travel, so even a shorter queue spends distance the release argument needs. No friction change is needed for this arithmetic to breach the clear-distance budget. The experiment must distinguish target appearance, capture, dispatch, admission, lease expiry, and powered response onset so that an interval is neither omitted nor counted twice.

**Local watchdogs verify component execution, not end-to-end physical propagation.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Enforce monotonic capture-to-torque evidence epoch tags across all processing nodes. Compare the sensor's physical capture timestamp directly with the permission path's decision tick, rejecting any proposal whose end-to-end latency budget is exceeded regardless of local thread heartbeats.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Allowing diagnostic logging and high-throughput telemetry to share fieldbuses with real-time safety loops.*

Real-time fieldbuses in physical AI (such as CAN FD and EtherCAT) are optimized for low-latency, deterministic control: EtherCAT cyclic Process Data Objects (PDOs) and CAN FD priority-arbitrated frames carry microsecond-accurate torque targets and lease-renewal heartbeats. When engineering teams attempt to capture rich diagnostic traces by multiplexing high-throughput telemetry, such as diagnostic memory core dumps, raw LiDAR point clouds, or uncompressed camera debug streams, through Ethernet-over-EtherCAT (EoE) or bulk CAN FD frames, they must bound the added traffic and processing demand to preserve command deadlines\index{Fieldbus!contention}.

In CAN FD, identifier priority governs arbitration, but an ongoing frame is not preempted by a newly ready higher-priority frame. Its blocking time depends on frame length, arbitration and data bit rates, and bit stuffing. Diagnostic bursts can therefore increase queueing and exhaust deadlines even when every transmitted frame is valid. Arbitration loss and high utilization alone do not increment CAN error counters. EtherCAT's master schedules cyclic traffic and acyclic mailbox traffic separately; mailbox use does not inherently delay process data. A faulty schedule or contention in shared host or slave processing resources can still compromise the implementation's deadline. Qualification must measure those resource paths under the admitted diagnostic load.

If diagnostic load delays a required renewal or drive update beyond its deadline, the affected watchdog must invoke the qualified local response. A stop request delayed on the same path can also consume clearance. The trial must witness both communication timing and physical response; observing a timeout alone does not show that the body stopped within its envelope.

**Unbudgeted diagnostic traffic can delay the commands and evidence needed for a bounded response.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Separate diagnostic telemetry from command traffic, or qualify a protocol-specific allocation: bounded frame lengths, identifiers, and ingress rates for CAN FD; a bounded cyclic/mailbox schedule and processing budget for EtherCAT. Ethernet TSN scheduling and frame preemption apply only on links and devices that implement those features; they are not a preemption mechanism for CAN FD or ordinary EtherCAT traffic.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Relying on software anomaly detectors that share electrical power or failure modes with monitored actuators.*

Motor acceleration, stall current, and regenerative braking can disturb the supply and references shared with digital transducers. Inverter switching produces inductive transients ($V = L\,dI/dt$); battery and wiring impedance can also pull the shared bus below a converter's usable input range. The F4 campaign specifies the injected rail waveform and measures its effect on each supposedly independent sensor and controller supply.

If the transducers tasked with observing actuator motion share a common power distribution board, ground plane, or unisolated buck converter with the motor gate drivers, the brownout transient propagates directly into the sensor's internal microcontroller. One fault to inject is a stale velocity register or frozen telemetry record that continues to produce structurally valid frames while its underlying measurement has stopped updating. A frozen position counter alone would instead imply zero speed to a receiver that derives velocity from successive positions; the test must specify which value froze and how the receiver uses it.

Suppose the stale velocity field continues to report `{python} RackEndVerification.v_aisle_str` while the drive continues executing a stale accelerating command. Correct checksums and a plausible reported speed cannot establish actual motion. A detector without an independent motion witness may miss the divergence; a detector with other valid measurements may expose it. The campaign must inject the stated telemetry and drive faults and retain external speed and position through the resulting stop. Neither overspeed nor a zero estimator residual follows from the electrical fault alone.

**A power fault that disrupts an actuator can simultaneously blind the sensor tasked with detecting it.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Provide galvanically isolated, held-up auxiliary power rails for safety-critical transducers and the safety microcontroller. Validate that sensors signal a fault in a way a valid reading cannot imitate, rather than latching plausible frozen values. A pull-down to 0 V does not qualify, because on a sensor whose range starts at 0 V that reading is a valid minimum, often zero speed or zero distance. Out-of-band signaling needs a live zero with separate fault bands, as in the NAMUR NE 43 convention for current-loop transmitters [@namurne43], or a digital status field protected by a rolling counter and checksum so that a frozen or repeated frame is detected [@autosare2e].

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Treating an unobservable test outcome where diagnostic loggers dropped packets as evidence of safety.*

During high-severity physical fault injection, such as a short circuit on a drive phase, a battery disconnect relay opening under full load, or high-frequency electromagnetic interference (EMI) coupled onto a fieldbus, radiated and conducted noise fills the test cell. The resulting ground bounce and inductive kickback can couple into the data acquisition (DAQ) harness, causing high-speed digitizers to lose clock synchronization, PCIe frame grabbers to overflow their ring buffers, or the host logging daemon to crash into a kernel panic.

Concurrently, the physical mobile base comes to rest: either its passive mechanical brakes engaged, its gearbox back-drove to a stall, or it drifted gently against the test aisle's mechanical end-stop buffer. In an undisciplined test campaign, observers look at the stopped machine and declare the run a "PASS" ("no crash occurred and the system reached rest"), while dismissing the missing telemetry as an irrelevant "instrumentation glitch" or repeating the trial until the logger manages to survive.

This practice introduces **survivorship bias**\index{Survivorship bias!verification}: the trials in which the logger crashed are likely those with the most severe electrical transients. The permission-path microcontroller may have hung in an exception handler without commanding any deceleration, and the base may have come to rest only against the test aisle's end-stop buffer. An unrecorded trial cannot show which path stopped the base, and a warehouse aisle has no end-stop buffer. The four-verdict model mandates that an unrecorded trial must be scored as `UNOBSERVABLE` and counted as an immediate test defect. The campaign reports the count of each verdict and every untested case. If it also reports $N_{\text{pass}} / N_{\text{total}}$, that completion statistic must not be confused with a failure-probability estimate from valid, independently scored trials. The test campaign cannot proceed until the instrumentation harness is galvanically hardened to survive the injected environment.

**Discarding unobservable trials conceals the exact vulnerability under test through survivorship bias.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Categorize any test run with dropped, incomplete, or corrupted evidence as `UNOBSERVABLE`, a primary defect of the test harness. Mandate that release audits require nonzero evidence capture across 100 percent of required trials before calculating statistical pass rates.

:::
## Summary {#sec-verification-summary}

The rack-end stopping claim begins as a distance and timing budget. Verification makes it testable by declaring the envelope points at which it must hold, including the coupled corners that one-variable sweeps miss, and by specifying for each fault the negated condition, the injection point, the expected detector, the bounded response, and an independent witness. A stalled proposer is therefore tested through powered deceleration onset and travel to rest, measured from the last valid renewal, even when its host heartbeat remains alive. An oracle fixed before the run scores each trial as `PASS`, `FAIL`, `INVALID`, or `UNOBSERVABLE`, and coverage is reported per dimension rather than as one percentage.

The fault list comes from inverting the design records, from working forward through the physical machine, from the authority cases, from shared causes that couple faults, and from adversaries who induce disturbances at the transducers. Some attacks touch no bus or sensor. An adversarial instruction on the task channel, or a patch or sign in the camera view, steers the learned proposer itself, so these proposer-injection attacks test the proposal boundary directly. The permission path cannot see what steered a proposal and catches it only when the motion breaches a measured limit. Such a trial therefore scores on the physical oracle, and every wrong action that stayed inside the envelope is recorded as a coverage deficit. Each fault goes to the qualification rung that contains its mechanism, because a simulator cannot sag a bus it does not model, and formal proof reaches the small permission path rather than the learned proposer. On hardware, injectors sit at the physical interfaces and every scored event is recorded on instruments that share neither clock nor supply with the machine. Signed temporal margins then direct search toward small margins, and a simulated margin transfers only after the sim-to-real discount. Importance sampling turns runs concentrated near failure into an operational rate only when the proposal is declared and every run is weighted, and tail models support only the claims their assumptions justify. A counterexample can reject a claim; failure to find one leaves the unsearched region open. The fault records carry that distinction into release, each beside its claim.

Eight relations carry the chapter's quantitative argument, and @tbl-15-key-equations records what each bounds or decides.

| Equation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | What it bounds or decides                                                                                                                                | Derived                                                            |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| $t_{\text{onset}} \le T_{\text{lease}} + T_{\text{tick}} + T_{\text{bus}} + T_{\text{act}}$, and $d_{\text{F1}}(v) = v\,(T_{\text{lease}} + T_{\text{tick}} + T_{\text{bus}} + T_{\text{act}}) + d_{\text{suffix}}(v) + \epsilon_{\text{track}}$ | F1's two precommitted predicates, measured from the last valid renewal; the capture-referenced budget subtotal cannot stand in for them                  | @eq-verification-f1-oracle                                         |
| $\lambda_{\text{unmitigated}} = \lambda_{\text{raw}}(1 - C_{\text{diag}})$, $\;n \ge \ln(1-C)/\ln C_{\text{diag}}$                                                                                                                               | The diagnostic coverage a rate target demands, and the zero-miss injections, sampled in proportion to the fault rates, that demonstrate it               | \ref{nbk-verification-hardware-fault-injection-coverage-mean-time} |
| $\Delta t = r_{\text{drift}}\,T_{\text{blackout}} + \sigma_{\text{jitter}}$                                                                                                                                                                      | How much of the clock-conversion bound behind F2's refusal threshold a synchronization blackout spends                                                   | @eq-verification-clock-drift                                       |
| $\rho(\square_{[0,T]}\phi) = \min_t \rho(\phi, s, t)$, $\;\rho(\lozenge_{[0,\tau]}\phi) = \max_t \rho(\phi, s, t)$                                                                                                                               | The signed margin of a trace against a temporal requirement, the score a falsifier drives toward zero                                                    | @eq-verification-stl-recursive-robustness                          |
| $\min_{\theta_0, \mathbf{p}} \rho(\phi, s(\theta_0, w(\mathbf{p})), 0)$ subject to $\lVert w \rVert_\infty \le \Delta_w$                                                                                                                         | The worst initial state and realizable disturbance a search can find; a search that finds none certifies nothing                                         | @eq-verification-adversarial-falsification                         |
| $\rho_{\text{real}} \ge \rho_{\text{sim}} - L_\phi\,\epsilon_{\text{gap}}$                                                                                                                                                                       | The physical margin a simulated margin guarantees, given a discrepancy bound justified over the claimed conditions                                       | @eq-verification-robustness-discount                               |
| $\hat{P}_F = \frac{1}{N}\sum_i \mathbb{1}[x_i \in F]\,w(x_i)$, $\;x_i \sim q$                                                                                                                                                                    | An operational failure rate from runs concentrated near failure, valid only with a declared $p$, a proposal that covers the failure set, and the weights | @eq-verification-importance-sampling                               |
| $z_{T, \text{sim}} + L_\phi\,\epsilon_{\text{gap}} \le d_{\text{clear}} - d_{\text{budget}}$                                                                                                                                                     | Whether a discounted tail estimate fits inside the physical reserve; a necessary check, not a release rule                                               | @eq-verification-evt-release-condition                             |

: **Key equations of adversarial verification**: The relations that turn a stopping budget into precommitted predicates, size a fault-injection campaign, and limit what search, simulation, and rare-event statistics can claim, with the place each is derived. {#tbl-15-key-equations tbl-colwidths="[40,42,18]"}

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ Untested operational regimes identified during falsification feed the epistemic boundary analysis in @sec-frontier-epistemic-limits.
:::

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Adversarial verification and fault injection"}
* **A fault tests a physical claim:** Derive the injection, detector, response, and independent witness from the stopping or contact bound. Successful task execution alone does not exercise the protective response.
* **The environment bounds the evidence:** Select each qualification rung for the mechanism it exercises. Simulation, processor execution, electrical benches, and physical rigs contribute complementary evidence with different blind spots.
* **Search finds counterexamples, not universal passes:** Signed temporal margins help prioritize disturbances near a violation. An unsuccessful search does not establish a global minimum, and a fitted tail does not prove a hard physical limit.
* **Precommitment preserves the meaning of a pass:** Fix conditions and predicates before injection. Keep `FAIL`, `INVALID`, and `UNOBSERVABLE` distinct, because missing or invalid evidence cannot support the stopping claim.
* **Verification hands release bounded evidence:** Bind each fault record to its claim, builds, conditions, and raw measurements. Coverage gaps and model assumptions remain part of the fault records, so release can restrict authority where evidence ends.

:::

Verification supports the evidence-bounds-authority principle by making the limits of each test part of its result. The illustrative stopping record still has no measured outcome. A complete record format cannot fill that gap; the specified physical trial must supply the evidence.
## Historical Perspective and Further Reading {#sec-verification-history}

Deliberate fault injection came from the dependability community of the 1980s, which forced faults onto the pins of working processors to learn whether error detection behaved as designed. @arlat1990fault built the MESSALINE tool on that idea and organized each campaign by the faults it injected, the activity that exercised them, the readouts it recorded, and the measures it derived, which is the skeleton of the fault record in this chapter. Later tools moved injection into software, and the survey of @hsueh1997fault set out the choice between hardware-implemented injection, which reaches fault locations software cannot touch, and software-implemented injection, which is cheaper and easier to control but reaches only what software can reach. The same trade runs through every rung of the qualification ladder. The community also learned early that observing a system can change its behavior, the probe effect that @gait1986probe named, which is why the witnesses in this chapter live on their own clocks and supplies.

The search methods have a separate lineage. @pnueli1977temporal brought temporal logic to program verification, @maler2004monitoring extended it to the real-valued signals of physical systems, and @fainekos2009robustness gave its formulas a signed margin, which turned verification into optimization. S-TaLiRo [@annpureddy2011staliro] and Breach [@donze2010breach] packaged that optimization for models of cyber-physical systems. Rare-event estimation is older still. Importance sampling came out of the Monte Carlo shielding calculations of the early 1950s [@kahn1953methods], the cross-entropy method made the proposal adaptive [@rubinstein2004cross], and @okelly2018scalable applied both to an autonomous-driving stack. Extreme value theory reached engineering through flood hydrology [@gumbel1958statistics] and gained its threshold form from @balkema1974residual and @pickands1975statistical.

Formal verification of learned components is the youngest strand. Reluplex [@katz2017reluplex] showed that a constraint solver could prove properties of small ReLU networks, and bound-propagation verifiers such as α,β-CROWN [@wang2021betacrown] have since carried that work to much larger networks, though still far smaller than a vision-language-action proposer. What this chapter adds is the discipline that binds these strands to one machine. Each trial tests a named claim, is scored by an oracle fixed before the run, is witnessed by instruments the fault cannot reach, and is kept as a record that carries its own coverage deficits to release.

For further reading, six works trace the lineage from dependability testing to validation algorithms.

- @arlat1990fault sets out fault injection as a designed experiment, with the faults, activation, readouts, and measures declared in advance, the form the fault record of @sec-verification-manifest-coverage follows.
- @leveson2011engineering develops STAMP and STPA, the hazard analysis that finds faults at interfaces where no component has failed, as @sec-verification-forward-analysis requires.
- @fainekos2009robustness defines the robustness of temporal logic formulas over continuous signals, the signed margin that @sec-verification-stl-robustness scores and searches.
- @owen2013monte treats importance sampling and its diagnostics with care, including the effective sample size and the ways a proposal can fail without any warning in the draws.
- @corso2021survey organizes black-box safety validation by what each method returns: a counterexample, the most likely failure, or a failure probability.
- @kochenderfer2026validation develops falsification, failure-probability estimation, reachability, and runtime monitoring as one algorithmic treatment of a declared system and property.
## Problems {#sec-verification-problems}

```{python}
#| label: calc-verify-problems
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ END-OF-CHAPTER PROBLEM GIVENS (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-verification-problems.
# │ Goal:    Print each problem's givens from the registry and the chapter's
# │          cells, and guard the property each problem depends on, so a
# │          registry change cannot silently turn an intended answer around.
# │ Show:    givens only (answers live in the private instructor solutions):
# │          a 1.2 m/s dry-floor point; a 95 ms / 790 mm trace; a 0.5 percent
# │          miss limit and 500 bench runs; 50 mm and 150 mm transfer bounds;
# │          a 25 percent drift share; a 10 ms mean queue delay; the Unitree H1
# │          top speed of 3.3 m/s; a supplier's 98 percent of 5,000 trials.
# │ How:     Reuses RackEndVerification, ClockDriftVerification, and
# │          RareEventOvershoot; recomputes each guarded property with the
# │          MLSysIM S-curve, zero-failure, and importance-sampling helpers.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import math
from mlsysim import Embodied
from mlsysim.core.units import ureg, millisecond, microsecond, second, meter, millimeter
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import calc_scurve_stop_distance, calc_zero_failure_sample_size
from mlsysim.physics import (
    calc_monte_carlo_sample_size,
    calc_importance_sampling_exponential,
    calc_cross_entropy_exponential_proposal,
)
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_int, fmt_latency, fmt_length, fmt_velocity, fmt_percent, check

H1 = Embodied.Humanoid.Unitree_H1

class VerificationProblems:
    """Givens for the Chapter 15 problems, with guards on the answers they imply."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    R = RackEndVerification  # category: derived; the chapter's oracle cell
    v_p1 = 1.2 * meter / second  # category: illustrative (problem given: a new dry-floor envelope point)
    p2_onset = 95 * millisecond  # category: illustrative (problem given: a stipulated trial outcome)
    p2_travel = 790 * millimeter  # category: illustrative (problem given: a stipulated trial outcome)
    p4_miss = 0.005  # category: illustrative (problem given: miss-probability limit)
    p4_bench = 500  # category: illustrative (problem given: deterministic bench runs)
    gap_a = 50 * millimeter  # category: illustrative (problem given: a validated discrepancy bound)
    gap_b = 150 * millimeter  # category: illustrative (problem given: a larger discrepancy bound)
    p6_share = 0.25  # category: illustrative (problem given: share of the clock-conversion bound)
    p7_mean = 10 * millisecond  # category: illustrative (problem given: mean queue delay)
    v_h1 = H1.max_velocity.to(meter / second)  # category: datasheet (registry: Unitree H1 top speed)
    vendor_n = 5000  # category: illustrative (problem given: a supplier's trial count)
    vendor_pass = 0.98  # category: illustrative (problem given: a supplier's pass fraction)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    # P1: F1 oracle and capture-referenced subtotal at the new point
    sfx_p1 = calc_scurve_stop_distance(v_p1, R.a_brake, R.j_brake).to(millimeter)
    f1_p1 = (v_p1 * R.onset_bound + sfx_p1 + R.eps_track).to(millimeter)
    sub_p1 = (v_p1 * R.tau_delay + sfx_p1 + R.overhead).to(millimeter)
    # P2: margins of the stipulated trace against the aisle-speed oracle
    rho_on_p2 = (R.onset_bound - p2_onset).to(millisecond)
    rho_d_p2 = (R.f1_aisle_stop_bound - p2_travel).to(millimeter)
    late_share_p2 = (R.v_aisle * (p2_onset - R.onset_bound)).to(millimeter)
    # P3: nominal-bus step to lockout; longest stop the hold-up covers; fastest inspected-floor stop that fits
    i_cross_nom = ((R.bus_nominal - R.bus_uvlo) / R.bus_r).to(ureg.ampere)
    t_stop_max = (R.rail_holdup - R.flag_onset - R.brake_engage_max).to(millisecond)
    v_hold_max = (R.a_insp * (t_stop_max - R.a_insp / R.j_brake)).to(meter / second)
    # P4: zero-miss count
    n_p4 = calc_zero_failure_sample_size(1.0 - p4_miss, confidence=0.95)
    # P5: discounted margins with L_phi = 1 in a 1 m position norm
    rho_real_a = (R.spare - gap_a).to(millimeter)
    rho_real_b = (R.spare - gap_b).to(millimeter)
    # P6: longest sync period whose four-period drift stays within the share
    rate = ClockDriftVerification.rate
    t_sync_max = (p6_share * R.eps_sync / (ClockDriftVerification.n_blackout * rate)).to(millisecond)
    # P7: importance sampling at the new mean
    ce7 = calc_cross_entropy_exponential_proposal(RareEventOvershoot.t_exhaust, p7_mean, RareEventOvershoot.elite_share)
    is7 = calc_importance_sampling_exponential(RareEventOvershoot.t_exhaust, p7_mean, ce7["proposal_mean"])
    p_f7 = is7["failure_probability"]
    n_mc7 = calc_monte_carlo_sample_size(p_f7, RareEventOvershoot.rel_err)
    n_is7 = is7["relative_variance"] / RareEventOvershoot.rel_err**2
    # P8: humanoid pre-onset travel and the lease that would match the warehouse machine
    pre_h1 = (v_h1 * R.onset_bound).to(millimeter)
    lease_h1 = (R.f1_preonset_aisle / v_h1 - (R.onset_bound - R.t_lease)).to(millisecond)
    # P11: the trials the pass fraction leaves unexplained
    vendor_other = round(vendor_n * (1 - vendor_pass))

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(f1_p1 < sub_p1 < R.d_clear, "P1: the oracle must sit below a subtotal that fits the clear distance.")
    check(
        abs((sub_p1 - f1_p1).magnitude - (v_p1 * R.t_age + R.delta_loc + R.delta_margin).to(millimeter).magnitude) < 1e-6,
        "P1: gap is age travel plus the two margins.",
    )
    check(
        rho_on_p2.magnitude < 0 and rho_d_p2.magnitude < 0 and late_share_p2 < -rho_d_p2,
        "P2: both margins fail and the late onset explains only part of the overrun.",
    )
    check(i_cross_nom > R.i_cross > R.i_rail, "P3: the nominal bus needs a larger step than the depleted one.")
    check(v_hold_max > R.v_drive, "P3: the hold-up covers any stop up to the drive limit, so it does not bind.")
    check(n_p4 == 598 and abs(n_p4 - 3 / p4_miss) < 3, "P4: 598 injections, close to 3/p = 600.")
    check(rho_real_a.magnitude > 0 > rho_real_b.magnitude, "P5: the smaller bound keeps a guaranteed margin; the larger does not.")
    check(abs(t_sync_max.magnitude - 62.5) < 1e-9 and t_sync_max < ClockDriftVerification.t_sync, "P6: 62.5 ms, shorter than the healthy period.")
    check(1e-5 < p_f7 < 1e-4 and n_is7 < n_mc7 / 100, "P7: a far likelier failure that importance sampling still estimates much faster.")
    check(pre_h1 > 2.5 * R.f1_preonset_aisle and lease_h1 < R.chunk_period, "P8: the humanoid needs a lease shorter than the chunk period.")
    check(vendor_other == 100, "P11: 100 trials not accounted as passes.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    v_p1_str = fmt_velocity(v_p1, precision=1)
    p2_onset_str = fmt_latency(p2_onset, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    p2_travel_str = fmt_length(p2_travel, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    p4_miss_pct_str = fmt_percent(p4_miss, precision=1)
    p4_bench_str = fmt_int(p4_bench)
    gap_a_str = fmt_length(gap_a, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    gap_b_str = fmt_length(gap_b, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    p6_share_pct_str = fmt_percent(p6_share, precision=0)
    p7_mean_str = fmt_latency(p7_mean, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    v_h1_str = fmt_velocity(v_h1, precision=1)
    vendor_n_str = fmt_int(vendor_n, commas=True)
    vendor_pass_pct_str = fmt_percent(vendor_pass, precision=0)
```

Each problem states its givens, which come from the machine card (@tbl-01-machine-card), from this chapter's calculations, or from the MLSysIM registry. A given marked illustrative is an assumption for the exercise, not a measurement, and a stipulated trial outcome is an exercise input, never a result of the machine. The tag names the kind of work, and the parenthesis names the learning objective the problem assesses.

1. **[Compute]** (Stopping oracles) Declare a new envelope point at `{python} VerificationProblems.v_p1_str` on a dry floor (illustrative). Using @eq-verification-f1-oracle, compute F1's onset and distance oracles there, then the capture-referenced subtotal of the design budget and the spare it leaves of the `{python} RackEndVerification.d_clear_str` clear distance. Which terms of the subtotal does the oracle omit, and for each one, what fault would have to be under test for that term to belong in the oracle?
2. **[Compute]** (Temporal margins) An F1 trial at `{python} RackEndVerification.v_aisle_str` records powered deceleration onset `{python} VerificationProblems.p2_onset_str` after the last valid renewal and `{python} VerificationProblems.p2_travel_str` of travel from that renewal to rest (a stipulated outcome). Compute both signed margins against the aisle-speed oracle, the normalized margins with the bounds themselves as scales, and the verdict. How much of the distance overrun does the late onset explain, and which instruments of @fig-15-f1-test-rig would you examine for the remainder?
3. **[Compute]** (Hardware injection) For F4a, find the current step that would carry the drive bus from its `{python} RackEndVerification.bus_nominal_str` nominal to the `{python} RackEndVerification.bus_uvlo_str` lockout through the `{python} RackEndVerification.bus_r_str` source resistance, and compare it with the step needed at the depleted point (\ref{nbk-verification-supply-headroom}). For F4b, find the longest stop the `{python} RackEndVerification.rail_holdup_str` hold-up can cover after the `{python} RackEndVerification.flag_onset_str` onset and the `{python} RackEndVerification.brake_engage_str` brake engagement, and the highest inspected-floor speed whose jerk-limited stop fits it. Decide whether the hold-up or the `{python} RackEndVerification.v_drive_str` drive limit binds, and what the F4b trial must therefore measure.
4. **[Compute]** (Transfer and rare events) How many zero-miss injections bound the miss probability at `{python} VerificationProblems.p4_miss_pct_str` percent with `{python} InjectedPopulationTrials.confidence_pct_str` percent confidence? Compare the count with the rule-of-three estimate. A team counts `{python} VerificationProblems.p4_bench_str` runs of one deterministic fault script on a digital bench (illustrative) toward that total. State how many independent trials those runs are worth and what must vary between repetitions for them to count.
5. **[Compute]** (Transfer and rare events) A simulated F1 stop at the aisle speed ends with the whole `{python} RackEndVerification.spare_str` reserve intact. With the distance predicate in meters and a 1 m position scale ($L_\phi = 1$), find the physical margin that @eq-verification-robustness-discount guarantees if the justified discrepancy bound is `{python} VerificationProblems.gap_a_str` and if it is `{python} VerificationProblems.gap_b_str` (both illustrative). The smaller bound was measured on an unloaded, cool machine. State what the record may claim for loaded, thermally throttled trials, and what paired measurement would extend it.
6. **[Compute]** (Hardware injection) With the illustrative oscillator limits of @sec-verification-clock-drift-sync, a worst relative rate of `{python} ClockDriftVerification.ppm_total_str` ppm, find the longest sync period that keeps the drift over a four-period blackout within `{python} VerificationProblems.p6_share_pct_str` percent of the `{python} RackEndVerification.eps_sync_str` clock-conversion bound. Does the healthy `{python} ClockDriftVerification.t_sync_str` period meet it? Decide whether to shorten the period or to budget a larger share of the bound, and describe the F2 trial that would expose a wrong choice.
7. **[Compute]** (Transfer and rare events) Repeat the rack-end example of @sec-verification-importance-sampling with a mean queue delay of `{python} VerificationProblems.p7_mean_str` (illustrative). Compute the operational probability that a stop overshoots the reserve, the plain Monte Carlo runs for `{python} RareEventOvershoot.rel_err_pct_str` relative error, the zero-failure count, and the runs an exponential cross-entropy proposal needs. Which estimate would you run, and what measurement must replace the assumed delay distribution before any of these numbers enters a fault record?
8. **[Compute]** (Stopping oracles, transfer to a humanoid) A Unitree H1 humanoid, whose registry top speed is `{python} VerificationProblems.v_h1_str`, runs the same permission path with the same lease path. Compute its travel before powered onset and compare it with the warehouse machine's at the aisle speed and with the `{python} RackEndVerification.d_clear_str` clear distance. What lease would hold that travel to the warehouse value, and is such a lease compatible with the `{python} RackEndVerification.chunk_period_str` chunk period? The registry carries no stopping deceleration for the H1. Name the measurement that must supply $d_{\text{suffix}}$ before a distance oracle can be written, and the assumption of the warehouse machine that the humanoid breaks.
9. **[Design]** (Fault derivation) Write the five-element chain for a new fault: the LiDAR's timestamp clock freezes while its point clouds keep arriving in well-formed packets. Name the negated condition, the physical injection point, the detector the design should already contain, the bounded response, and a pass condition with its reference event and independent witness. State which rung of the qualification ladder must run the trial, and why a lower one cannot.
10. **[Design]** (Qualification environments) For F2, F3, the actuator jam, A3, and the proposer-injection row of @tbl-15-fault-classification, choose the lowest rung that contains the causal mechanism and name one mechanism that rung still idealizes away. For each trial, state which elements of the causal loop its report must list as physically real, simulated, replayed, bypassed, or unobserved.
11. **[Critique]** (Fault records) A supplier reports that `{python} VerificationProblems.vendor_pass_pct_str` percent of `{python} VerificationProblems.vendor_n_str` fault trials passed (illustrative) and asks for the figure to enter the release case. Write the review. State which verdict counts and coverage dimensions must accompany the figure, what the trials that did not pass could conceal, and why a pass fraction is not a failure-probability estimate.
12. **[Critique]** (Transfer and rare events) An engineer fits a generalized Pareto distribution with negative shape to the overshoots a simulated falsification campaign found, and reports its finite endpoint as the maximum stopping overshoot, well inside the `{python} RackEndVerification.spare_str` reserve. Give the reasons the endpoint cannot fill the F1 record's outcome field, and specify what the campaign would need, in sampling, weighting, fit uncertainty, and transfer, before a return level could be checked against the reserve with @eq-verification-evt-release-condition.

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From verification to release decisions"}
Verification hands release the fault records and the coverage gaps they expose. For each claim, they bind the relevant qualification manifests and fault records, together with any sim-to-real bounds ($\epsilon_{\text{gap}}$) or tail estimates on which the claim relies. They distinguish measured margins, conditional estimates, and regimes no trial reaches. No record yet carries a measured verdict, so none says whether the machine may drive the aisle. @Sec-release takes these fault records, together with the authority, placement, and evaluation records, and evaluates which claims they support, which operational verdict follows (`UNCOND`, `COND`, or `REFUSE`), and which standing conditions must govern deployment.
:::
